event.name: Pipeline After the Webinar: Turning Event Engagement into Revenue

batches.subject_a: The 3.2x stat from today's session (and your takeaways)
batches.subject_b: Priya, Daniel & Sara's follow-up: your recording + 3 takeaways

contactProperties.name: takeaway_headline
contactProperties.value: Multi-threading is already happening — most teams just don't see it.

contactProperties.name: takeaway_body
contactProperties.value: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) flagged that accounts with three or more attendees on the same webinar convert to opportunity at almost double the rate of single-attendee accounts — worth checking your own account list for this event. [25:04] Per Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point ([26:15]), the version of this worth your attention outside pure enterprise software leads with time-to-value and pricing rather than integration depth — that's the objection he flagged as the real one at smaller or less software-native shops. [26:52]

contactProperties.name: takeaway_headline
contactProperties.value: Subject lines aren't a rounding error.

contactProperties.name: takeaway_body
contactProperties.value: Daniel Kim (Northwind Analytics) A/B tested two attendee thank-you subject lines — one led with the speaker's name, one led with a specific stat — and the stat-led version won by about 14 percentage points on open rate. [18:15] Daniel Kim's point about a fourth personalization layer, industry and company size, is worth applying literally here: he described leading enterprise-tier takeaways with integration and security rather than pricing, since that's usually the actual blocker on a software deal. [26:52]

contactProperties.name: takeaway_body
contactProperties.value: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) shared that moving from one blanket post-webinar email to attendee/no-show/speaker segmentation — plus role-based variants — took overall click-through from about 6% to just over 17%, without changing send timing at all. [28:20] If you're running this across client accounts at an IT-services or agency shop, Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point ([26:15]) is exactly why we didn't send you one generic recap — which part is worth your time depends on which client this session was actually for.
